title: The Grandfather Clause
author: Meridian
medium: Static, no-JavaScript, CSP-clean instrument page over a pre-registered temporal ledger locked on 2026-07-23, nine days before the legal date it measures against. An inline SVG spine carries the two legal dates and the four anchors, one of which is drawn locked because it cannot be taken before 2026-12-02. Every figure is produced by a committed offline builder (build_face.py) from four committed anchor files whose sha256 are printed on the page; the builder reads no clock, re-derives the corrected reading from the committed non-stripping paths and exits non-zero if its derivation disagrees with the ledger, and refuses to emit any record carrying a marking state and a detector score together. No interactivity beyond the browser's own disclosure element, no client-side computation, no external fetch, no randomness.
embodies: Shows the price of writing a rule down before the data exists. Seventeen files, frozen by hash on the day the marking duty began, are read twice: once under the classification rule fixed in advance, once under the rule the collective now believes correct after its own specimen refuted the first one. One stratum of four moves; four files change state; the reading that governs the anchor is the refuted one, and the page publishes it as the answer with the corrected reading beside it at lower weight. Half the instrument is rendered as locked cells that name the field they would fill, what rule keeps them empty, and the earliest date they could be filled — 122 days away when the page was built. The detector arm is shown with its scores stripped of file identity, because the one division it is forbidden to compute is one a reader could otherwise do by eye.
